meta.title: AI Bubble Tracker
meta.thesis: The AI capex/circular-financing structure fails not when the numbers fall — it fails when they stop accelerating. Watch the speed, not the level.
meta.crisisFrame: 2006: loans failed when prices rose 8% instead of 15%. Watch the speed.

verdict.compositeNote: Big Tech's AI spending and order books are still growing faster every year — and that growth is the only thing holding the whole structure up. Warning signs: OpenAI's next fundraise is expected to value it at only about 1.2x its last round (every earlier round was 1.7-1.9x), and free Chinese models are eating into the revenue growth that justifies those valuations. The event that would mark the turn hasn't happened yet. The lesson of 2006: this structure doesn't need the numbers to fall — it breaks as soon as they stop growing faster each year. Independent corroboration (Eisman, Aug 13): AI infrastructure earnings still accelerating — CoreWeave revenue +112% YoY (still unprofitable), Super Micro +91%, Cisco beat and raised — but a new $500B Nvidia securitization push moves data-center debt off hyperscaler balance sheets into banks and private credit, the most literal 2006 rhyme yet.

stack.requirement: Leases stay current + structures keep finding buyers

stepUpLadder.name: The Step-Up Ladder
stepUpLadder.question: Does OpenAI's next raise price above the last, and by how much?

nextExpected.note: Smallest step-up ever — at the exact moment free Chinese models attack the growth that justifies it

notes.text: The step-up multiple IS the collateral. Like 2006 house prices, the ladder doesn't need to fall to break the structure — it just needs to stop climbing at the required rate.
notes.attribution: Jay Martin, The Jay Martin Show

backlog.name: The Backlog
backlog.question: Do the backlogs keep GROWING, or do they just stay large? Not the same thing.

concentration.note: ~50% owed by OpenAI + Anthropic — neither profitable. >50% of Oracle's backlog traces to OpenAI alone. Research-firm estimates (via Eisman, Aug 2026): ~70% of hyperscaler AI revenue and 25–35% of total cloud revenue comes from Anthropic + OpenAI.

backlog.trigger: Backlog growth rate declines two consecutive quarters = decelerating; flat/shrinking = broken
backlog.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); platform earnings backlogs (RPO)

notes.text: The dependency of the hyperscalers on Anthropic and OpenAI is just huge — both lose billions and rely on raising capital for survival. Oracle's debt is rated barely above junk. There is no hedge for the LLMs: hyperscalers have fallback franchises, the labs don't.
notes.attribution: Steve Eisman, The Real Eisman Playbook

capex.name: Capex Acceleration
capex.question: The day the market rewards a company for LEAVING the race is the day the race is over.
capex.keyFact: 2026: first year construction spend exceeds combined operating cash flow of the four platforms — every marginal dollar is debt-funded, borrowed against backlog owed by unprofitable borrowers

killTrigger.description: A tech giant announces it is cutting AI data-center spending — and its share price goes UP on the news
killTrigger.explainer: Right now investors treat every extra billion of AI spending as good news, so cutting back would normally hurt a stock. The day the market cheers a company for spending less, investors have stopped believing the race is worth winning. That is the clearest early sign the boom is turning — it would show up long before any crash.

capex.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); hyperscaler capex guidance

notes.text: Nvidia's $500B securitized-financing push means some data-center capex shifts off hyperscaler cash flow — hyperscaler FCF 'could improve' optically while the debt stack extends into banks and private credit. Read improving FCF with suspicion from here.
notes.attribution: Steve Eisman, The Real Eisman Playbook

notes.text: Kill-trigger watch candidate: Meta is getting squeezed — latest quarter revenue +28% but expenses +55%, no cloud business to monetize AI through. Most likely first major player to cut; watch how the market reacts when it does.
notes.attribution: Steve Eisman, The Real Eisman Playbook

chinaShare.name: China Share Pressure
chinaShare.question: Chinese models don't need to be better. Nearly as good and nearly free is enough.

events.text: Moonshot releases Kimi K3 — #1 on coding leaderboard within a day, beating Anthropic and OpenAI blind at ~40% lower cost
Kimi K3 open-sourced — free to download and self-host

chinaShare.mechanism: Pulls customers away AND forces down prices American labs can charge — both push on the speed of US AI revenue growth. The speed is the collateral.

notes.text: Red here does not mean Chinese models are failing — it means pressure against US share is RISING. This signal measures the force pushing on US revenue speed.

policyWatch.name: Policy Watch
policyWatch.question: Ban or no ban — either path stresses the structure.
policyWatch.headline: Washington debating emergency ban on Chinese AI; David Sacks: 'this is concerning'
policyWatch.interpretation: The catfish effect run backwards — China used competition to grow strong; a US ban removes the pressure that forces improvement while cutting US businesses off from a nearly-free tool. Either path stresses the structure: ban → protected stagnation; no ban → growth curve flattens.
policyWatch.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); Washington policy debate coverage

treasuryStack.name: The Treasury Stack
treasuryStack.question: In the next crisis, the fear points AT the belief that funds the Treasury.
treasuryStack.interestVsDefense: Interest now exceeds the entire military budget
treasuryStack.watch: Auction bid-to-cover + 10Y behavior during AI-led selloffs: in 2008 scared money BOUGHT treasuries (fear pointed at banks). An AI crash points fear at the belief in American growth itself — scared money may walk.
treasuryStack.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); US Treasury data

securitization.name: Compute Securitization Watch
securitization.question: When compute becomes securitized collateral, who ends up holding the paper — and does the remittance data start publishing?

deal.structure: Nvidia partnering with six large asset managers on a $500B financing push treating AI data centers like commercial real estate or toll roads — structure unclear, securitizations assumed
deal.shift: Until now AI data centers were financed by hyperscaler cash flow and corporate debt. This moves some financing into securitized paper held by banks and private credit.

securitization.interpretation: The most literal 2006 rhyme yet: debt collateralized by payments owed largely by two unprofitable borrowers (OpenAI and Anthropic), relocating off hyperscaler balance sheets into banks and private credit. Watch for a masking effect — hyperscaler free cash flow can LOOK better while the risk relocates rather than shrinks.
securitization.metaNote: Eisman shorted subprime because Moody's securitization database published monthly delinquency data. He says no such dataset exists for AI. If these deals securitize, monthly remittance data on compute-lease payments would eventually become exactly that dataset — the first real credit tape for the AI buildout.
